Book of Utilities

book.of.utilities seeks to facilitate execution of those repetitive, ad-hoc tasks often encountered during data processing.

Installation

Use remotes::install_github("delriaan/book.of.utilities", subdir = "pkg") to install the latest version from GitHub.

Functions

The following functional families are covered in book.of.utilities:

Chapter 1: Calculators

Function Synopsis
calc.means() Calculates one or more mean variants (arithmetic, zero, geometric, harmonic, RMS) for vectors and tabular inputs. Supports optional post-processing and z-score transformation.
calc.zero_mean() Returns values centered at zero by subtracting the mean. Can optionally scale output as z-scores.
calc.rms() Computes the root-mean-square of numeric input. This is a convenience wrapper around calc.means().
calc.harmonic_mean() Computes the harmonic mean of numeric input. This is a convenience wrapper around calc.means().
calc.geo_mean() Computes the geometric mean of numeric input. This is a convenience wrapper around calc.means().
ratio() Computes ratio-based transforms such as relative-to-sum, relative-to-max, or cumulative ratio. Supports optional sorting and density-style transformation.
ranking.algorithm() Assigns rank values to scores using threshold mapping logic. Can return mapping metadata and optionally process via a configurable mapper.
range_diff() Returns the inclusive range width, computed as max minus min. Supports single vectors or lists of vectors.
odds2probs() Converts odds representations to probabilities. Accepts numeric vectors, log-odds, and colon-delimited string formats.

Chapter 2: Counters

Function Synopsis
count_cycles() Generates a cycle counter driven by a logical condition vector. Supports reset rules and custom starting offsets.
factor_int() Computes integer factors for one or more numeric inputs. Returns a vector or list depending on input length.
radix() Converts numeric representations across radix bases (for example binary, decimal, hexadecimal). Supports named bases and arbitrary numeric bases.
factor.int() Alias for factor_int().
count.cycles() Alias for count_cycles().

Chapter 3: Miscellaneous

Function Synopsis
log_note() Appends timestamped note text to a file or console. Can also display saved file contents.
vlogical() Performs vectorized pattern matching across one or more patterns. Returns a logical matrix or simplified column-wise summaries.
polyname2orig() Rewrites polynomial feature names back to source-variable form. Useful for making model matrix column names interpretable.
gen_primes() Generates prime numbers within a supplied domain. Supports random sampling and distinct-only output.
call_recursion() Repeatedly applies a function while a test condition is true, up to a maximum iteration count. Can return final output only or full iteration history.
checksum() Compares an object digest to an expected hash value. Supports file-based and object-based checks.
gen.primes() Alias for gen_primes().
call.recursion() Alias for call_recursion().

Chapter 4: Operators

Function Synopsis
%bin% Bins numeric values to fixed intervals using modulo subtraction. Stores binning ratio metadata as an attribute.
%><% Operator wrapper for test_between() to evaluate interval overlap or containment logic.
%tf% Creates paired true/false value choices for downstream conditional selection. Returns a two-column table structure.
%?% Applies simple if-then-else selection using a logical condition vector and provided true/false result set.
%??% Performs correlated row-wise conditional selection, returning matched true/false results for each row.
%if_na_empty% Replaces NA or empty values in one object using values from another object.
test_between() Tests whether ranges or values are between target ranges, with optional temporal labeling (before, during, after).

Chapter 5: Object Management

Function Synopsis
distinct.list() Returns first-level unique list elements using serialized hash signatures. Can return either a logical selector or filtered list.
enlist() Converts vectors to named lists, using provided names or value-derived defaults. Preserves existing names when present.
get.object_sizes() Recursively inspects environments and reports object sizes with depth information. Useful for memory profiling nested objects.
